purpose: The ways a running c++ program can HOLD layer-1 content. Not layer 1 (the data is fixed), not layer 3 (no operations beyond load-and-read-back), not the type system.
reference: language knowledge, checked against ../type_vocabulary/raw/cpp.types.json as a candidate checklist only (superseded node; not a decision instrument).

nothing.note: a type with exactly one value, the variant-library way to spell a case that carries nothing.
the null pointer value itself; it holds no pointee and no other content.
absence as a case of a two-case optional holder, so the hole still carries a declared element kind.

truth.note: two values, no numeric side in the source spelling.

whole.note: signed 32-bit; the narrow end, silently wraps values that do not fit.
unsigned 64-bit; reaches u64 max, refuses anything below zero.
signed 128-bit GNU extension; wide enough for every edge in the data file, but has no std::to_string so read-back is hand-rolled.
whole.read: [&]{ __int128 t = v; bool neg = t < 0; unsigned __int128 u = neg ? (unsigned __int128)(-(t+1)) + 1 : (unsigned __int128)t; std::string s; if (u==0) s = "0"; while (u > 0) { s += char('0' + (int)(u % 10)); u /= 10; } if (neg) s += '-'; std::reverse(s.begin(), s.end()); return s; }()

fractional.note: IEEE double, the ordinary fractional holder.
fractional.read: [&]{ std::ostringstream oss; oss << std::setprecision(17) << v; return oss.str(); }()

fractional.note: IEEE single; holds every base value at lower precision.
fractional.read: [&]{ std::ostringstream oss; oss << std::setprecision(9) << v; return oss.str(); }()

text.note: owned utf-8-ish byte string, growable, the ordinary text holder.
a view of a string literal baked into the binary; the pointer form.
text held as one array element per codepoint rather than per byte; read back as a codepoint list since it has no native utf-8 decoder.
text.read: [&]{ std::string s; for (char32_t c : v) { s += "[" + std::to_string((unsigned long)c) + "]"; } return s; }()

sequence.note: growable ordered run, one declared element kind.
sequence.read: [&]{ std::ostringstream oss; oss<<"["; bool first=true; for (auto& e : v) { if(!first) oss<<","; oss<<e; first=false; } oss<<"]"; return oss.str(); }()

sequence.note: fixed length baked into the type; a zero-length array is not legal standard c++, so the empty probe is expected to refuse.
sequence.read: [&]{ std::ostringstream oss; oss<<"["; for (size_t i=0;i<vn;++i){ if(i) oss<<","; oss<<v[i]; } oss<<"]"; return oss.str(); }()

probes.mixed: int64_t v[5] = {1, "two", 3.0, true, nullptr}; size_t vn = 5;

sequence.note: a fixed-length run that, unlike a raw c array, is allowed to be zero length.
sequence.read: [&]{ std::ostringstream oss; oss<<"["; bool first=true; for (auto& e : v) { if(!first) oss<<","; oss<<e; first=false; } oss<<"]"; return oss.str(); }()

sequence.note: ordered run open at both ends.
sequence.read: [&]{ std::ostringstream oss; oss<<"["; bool first=true; for (auto& e : v) { if(!first) oss<<","; oss<<e; first=false; } oss<<"]"; return oss.str(); }()

sequence.note: ordered run with cheap insertion anywhere, no random access.
sequence.read: [&]{ std::ostringstream oss; oss<<"["; bool first=true; for (auto& e : v) { if(!first) oss<<","; oss<<e; first=false; } oss<<"]"; return oss.str(); }()

sequence.note: fixed length, and each position may be a different kind; the one c++ sequence holder that takes the mixed row without complaint.
sequence.read: std::apply([](auto&&... args){ std::ostringstream oss; oss<<"("; bool first=true; auto pr=[&](auto&& a){ if(!first) oss<<","; using AT=std::decay_t<decltype(a)>; if constexpr (std::is_null_pointer_v<AT>) oss<<"null"; else oss<<a; first=false; }; (pr(args), ...); oss<<")"; return oss.str(); }, v)

probes.mixed: auto v = std::make_tuple((int64_t)1, std::string("two"), 3.0, true, nullptr);

keyed.note: name to element, kept in sorted key order.
the same grouping held with no guaranteed iteration order; read back sorts keys to make the probe reproducible.
keyed.read: [&]{ std::vector<std::string> ks; for (auto& kv : v) ks.push_back(kv.first); std::sort(ks.begin(), ks.end()); std::ostringstream oss; bool first=true; for (auto& k : ks) { if(!first) oss<<","; oss<<k<<"="<<dbg(v.at(k)); first=false; } return oss.str(); }()

keyed.note: field names are fixed when the shape is written, not when the data arrives; the odd keys are not spellable as field names at all.

probes.empty: struct R0 { std::string dbgstr() const { return ""; } }; R0 v = {};
probes.flat: struct R3 { int64_t a,b,c; std::string dbgstr() const { return "a="+std::to_string(a)+",b="+std::to_string(b)+",c="+std::to_string(c); } }; R3 v = {1,2,3};
probes.intlike: struct RI { int64_t 1; int64_t b; std::string dbgstr() const { return ""; } }; RI v = {1,2};
probes.emptykey: struct RE { std::string ; std::string dbgstr() const { return ""; } }; RE v = {"empty-string key"};
probes.nested: struct RN { std::vector<int64_t> outer; std::string dbgstr() const { std::string s="outer=["; for (size_t i=0;i<outer.size();++i){ if(i) s+=","; s+=std::to_string(outer[i]); } return s+"]"; } }; RN v = { {1,2} };

nesting.note: nesting by repeating the same holder; every level must carry the same declared element kind.
a hand-written sum shape; the only c++ holder here that takes every layer-1 form in one element position, which is what mixed-depth nesting needs.

probes.seq_in_seq: Node v{ std::vector<Node>{ Node{std::vector<Node>{Node{(int64_t)1}, Node{(int64_t)2}}}, Node{std::vector<Node>{Node{(int64_t)3}, Node{(int64_t)4}}} } };
probes.seq_in_map: Node v{ std::map<std::string,Node>{ {"outer", Node{std::map<std::string,Node>{ {"inner", Node{std::vector<Node>{Node{(int64_t)1}, Node{(int64_t)2}}} } }} } } };
probes.mixed_depth: Node v{ std::vector<Node>{ Node{(int64_t)1}, Node{std::vector<Node>{Node{(int64_t)2}, Node{std::map<std::string,Node>{{"k", Node{std::string("t")}}}}}}, Node{true}, Node{std::monostate{}} } };

identity.note: the ordinary owned holder; a value sits in only one position, so a second position needs a copy. Self-containment is impossible by construction, so the honest cycle attempt just copies the (empty) current state into itself rather than refusing to compile.
reference-counted sharing with mutation visible through every holder; the c++ shape a shared node and a cycle both need, at the cost of a leak if the cycle is never broken.
sharing and cycles like a shared pointer, but with no automatic lifetime management at all; the low-level holder underneath the others.
